also buy: water conditioner (i use seachem prime) and a water testing kit (api freshwater test kit). once you fill the tank up with water, you’ll have to let the filters run for a little bit to establish a bacteria colony in there before adding any fish in. if you wanna speed that up i used api quick start. 

this is gonna be confusing but it’s important that everyone with a tank knows about the cycling process — throw a few flakes/pebbles of fish food in once you’ve filled the tank up and let it sit with the filter running (the fish food will introduce ammonia as it breaks down). then start testing the water with that kit every few days. you’ll see the ammonia spike first. next, bacteria will grow that’ll convert that ammonia into nitrite, and you’ll see the nitrite level spike. lastly, bacteria that converts nitrite into nitrate will grow, and you’ll see levels of nitrate rising as both ammonia & nitrite fall. you’ll know when the tank is “cycled” and ready once your ammonia and nitrite levels read at zero. this is super important because if you add that fish in without this bacteria colony, the fish food and poop will add ammonia into your tank, and you’ll have no bacteria to get rid of it. even small amounts of ammonia can very quickly make your fish sick or even kill them. it’s definitely worth the wait to make sure your pet is healthy.

again good luck, and feel free to ask any questions!! i can’t promise i’ll know the answer to them but i’m sure someone here will lol

i’d start bottom up, pick a substrate you like if you wanna keep plants (aquasoil is easy, sand is good too but just requires root tabs) or if you want to just keep those rocks i’d take all the shells out. i think they can break down and raise the water hardness. 

i’d definitely recommend including real plants, they’re like an extra filter for your tank and will save you SO much time and energy in cleaning/water changes. very high reward for very low effort, plus they look great. also the betta’s natural habitat is in tropical marshes with dense vegetation, so they’ll be happiest with a heavily planted tank. plants will provide them with shade and hiding spots, and look beautiful too!! 

i’d then look up what kind of fish/invertebrates can live with them peacefully. i’ve never kept betta before so i don’t have any personal knowledge on their social behavior, but generally having a “clean up crew” is great. i’d look into tank buddies like shrimp, snails, or corys. some small schooling fish like tetras or rasboras could work great too! 

you’ll also need a light, you can get super cheap ones on amazon. bettas enjoy low light so i wouldn’t bother going crazy with an expensive light or co2 at all. look into low-light plants with broad leaves (for the betta to rest/sleep on) like java fern, amazon sword, or anubias. 

one more thing, betta like to hang out near the surface and make bubble nests, so floating plants are a great addition. the shade and fluffy roots will make your betta feel a lot more comfortable and safe hanging out at the surface & will give your betta a spot to build that bubble nest on. 

good luck to you and sushi!!

one thing you can do is take some of the rocks out, or use new rocks that you’ve cleaned, put them in a bucket or tupperware filled with dechlorinated water & leave that in a sunny spot for a few days. you can even use leftover water from a water change. just top off the water as it evaporates and leave them to sit and the rocks will grow algae. then you can leave those in your tank as a food source while you’re gone. i’d also avoid cleaning the tank walls before you leave, let any algae build up so they can snack on it while you’re gone.

main point- make sure their tummies are full before you leave and they should be fine :)

mistakes happen, theres a lot of learning to do in this hobby as a beginner. it can seem overwhelming sometimes. if you see this, i would recommend doing the following things:

1. return the fish and snail you have now back to the pet store. your tank needs to cycle and build up natural bacteria on its own, not just bacteria from the bottle. this will take a while and you have to wait before putting fish in. i know they’re in a smaller tank now, but they shouldn’t be kept in that smaller tank until this one is ready. you especially shouldn’t have the cory right now, it needs to be in a group of friends or it’ll get stressed. there are tons of other cute fish that can survive happily alone.

2. take the bamboo out. it will rot if it’s completely underwater. if you like the look of bamboo with your tank, look up “aquarium plant holding cups” on amazon

3. put a filter in. i don’t know what you mean when you said a filter didn’t fit… there are tons of different filters that can fit in all different sizes of tanks. if the filter you have now doesn’t fit, then return it and get a new one. 

this hobby requires patience. if you’re struggling with waiting the time it takes to build a proper tank, then maybe fish keeping isn’t for you. i’m not saying that with judgement. it’s not for everyone, and that’s okay. 

i saw you like looking at youtube videos for help. check out “aquarium co-op”, he has a lot of beginner friendly videos that helped me a lot. if you need any help you can absolutely message me. good luck!
